data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Eph total 20, reducing to 2. Number 2 is associated with cooperation, sensitivity and balance.

in_hebrew.name: אף
in_hebrew.long_meaning: The Hebrew name Eph is derived from the Hebrew letter 'אפ' (Ayin Peh), which represents the sounds 'f' and 'p'. This name is believed to have been derived from the Hebrew word 'אפה' (apheh), which means 'anger' or 'fury'. In the Bible, the name Eph is used for various individuals, including Ephraim, one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

in_latin.name: Eph
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin name Eph is derived from the Latin word 'effusus', which means 'gushing forth' or 'pouring out'. In the context of the Bible, this name may be a translation of the Hebrew name Eph, which means 'anger' or 'fury', and may symbolize the outpouring of God's wrath or the expression of human anger.

biblical_reference.note: In the Bible, the name Eph is most notably associated with Ephraim, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Ephraim is identified as the son of Joseph and Asenath, and is described as the elder brother of Manasseh. Ephraim is also referred to as 'the house of Joseph' or 'the house of Israel'. The territory allotted to the tribe of Ephraim includes the area around Bethel and Shechem.
